methods.name: Create
methods.description:
Create and trigger a new run: a turn in an existing session,
 or the first turn of a new one created from session_spec.

 A session works on one turn at a time. A turn in a session that already
 has an unfinished turn (pending, in progress, waiting for an answer or
 paused), or messages queued for the turn they start, is refused: send
 the message with sendMessage, which queues it.

 ## Error Conditions

 - FAILED_PRECONDITION with a google.rpc.ErrorInfo detail (domain
   "stigmer.ai", reason SESSION_TURN_UNFINISHED, metadata session_id):
   another turn of the session is unfinished, or messages wait for
   their turn

methods.name: SendMessage
methods.description:
Send a message to a session: the turn starts now, or the message waits
 for the turn that is working.

 run is the turn as create takes it, in an existing session
 (spec.session_id). When no turn of the session is unfinished, the turn
 starts at once, exactly as create starts it, and the reply names it.
 While a turn works, the message is queued instead: its user.message is
 stored with no processed_at and no run_id, and the reply carries it.
 The working turn reads it, or, once that turn has ended, the next turn
 starts with every message still queued, in the order sent: their texts
 joined, their files together, with the settings of the newest. A
 message read is listed once, where the agent read it, with its
 processed_at and the run that read it; it streams a second time as it
 moves there.

 A queued message meets every check a turn meets when it is sent, and
 the turn it starts meets them again. Stopping the session (interrupt,
 or terminating a turn) drops the messages still queued: they stay
 listed with no processed_at. A turn that cannot start (its agent was
 removed since, or a check refuses it) leaves them so too, and the
 session records the reason as a session.error.

 ## Error Conditions

 - FAILED_PRECONDITION with a google.rpc.ErrorInfo detail (domain
   "stigmer.ai", metadata session_id and run_id): reason
   SESSION_TURN_WAITS_FOR_ANSWER while a turn of the session waits for
   an answer (allow or deny it first; a deny can carry a message), or
   SESSION_TURN_PAUSED while one is paused (resume it first)
 - FAILED_PRECONDITION: spec names no existing session
 - every refusal create answers

methods.name: Update
methods.description:
Update a run: the fields update_mask names change, every other
 field keeps its stored value.

 resource.metadata.id names the run; apply finds one by slug. The slug
 changes only through rename, and a mask naming a field another door
 owns, or a path the run does not have, is refused with
 INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the path.

 An update is refused with ABORTED carrying a google.rpc.ErrorInfo detail
 (domain "stigmer.ai"):

   - ETAG_MISMATCH — resource.metadata.etag is set and the run changed
     since that etag was read: read it again and make the change again.
     No metadata.
   - WRITE_CONFLICT — the run kept changing while the update was
     being saved: try again. No metadata.

methods.name: Terminate
methods.description:
Terminate a run immediately.

 Force-stops the run without allowing cleanup. Unlike the session's
 interrupt, the agent cannot respond to termination - it is stopped immediately.
 Use this for stuck or unresponsive agents. The messages still queued in
 the run's session (sendMessage) are dropped with it: they stay listed,
 never read.

methods.name: Recover
methods.description:
Recover a failed run.

 Retries the failed run. Completed work is preserved - successful tool
 calls are NOT re-executed.

methods.name: Pause
methods.description:
Pause a running run.

 Temporarily stops the agent at its current checkpoint. Unlike the
 session's interrupt, the run is NOT terminal and can be resumed later from where it left off.

methods.name: Resume
methods.description:
Resume a paused run.

 Continues the run from where it was paused. How a turn's state is saved
 is the harness's ([Harnesses](/docs/concepts/harnesses)).

methodTypes.name: TerminateRunInput
methodTypes.description:
TerminateRunInput requests immediate termination of a run.

 Termination forcefully stops the run without allowing cleanup.
 Unlike an interrupt, the agent cannot respond to termination - it is stopped
 immediately. Use this for stuck or unresponsive runs. The run moves to
 RUN_TERMINATED at once, and any tool call in progress is stopped abruptly.

 ## Preconditions

 - Run must be in RUN_PENDING or RUN_IN_PROGRESS phase
 - User must have can_edit permission on the run

 ## Idempotency

 If the run is already terminated (phase == RUN_TERMINATED),
 the call succeeds as a no-op and returns the current run state.

 ## Terminated vs Cancelled

 | Aspect | Interrupt (session) | Terminate |
 |--------|--------|-----------|
 | Signal | The agent is told to stop | Nothing is sent |
 | Cleanup | The turn ends cleanly | No cleanup possible |
 | Use case | Normal cancellation | Stuck/unresponsive agents |
 | Recovery | Cannot recover | Cannot recover |

 ## Use Cases

 - Agent is stuck and not responding to cancellation
 - Agent is in an infinite loop
 - Emergency stop for misbehaving agent
 - Agent has a bug causing it to ignore cancellation signals

 ## Example

 {
   "id": "run_abc123xyz456",
   "reason": "Agent stuck in infinite loop, not responding to cancel"
 }

fields.name: Id
fields.description:
Run ID to terminate.

 Format: "run_{ulid}" (auto-generated unique identifier)
 Example: "run_abc123xyz456"

 Validation: Required, cannot be empty

fields.name: Reason
fields.description:
Human-readable reason for termination.

 Stored in the audit trail for operational debugging.
 Optional but strongly recommended - termination is a drastic action
 and the reason helps with post-incident analysis.

 Examples:
 - "Agent stuck for 30 minutes, not responding to cancel"
 - "Infinite loop detected in tool calls"
 - "Emergency stop - agent making unexpected API calls"
 - "Cancel failed after 3 attempts, force terminating"

methodTypes.name: RecoverRunInput
methodTypes.description:
RecoverRunInput requests recovery of a failed run.

 Recovery retries the failed run while preserving all completed work. The
 agent continues from where it failed without re-executing successful steps.
 The run moves from RUN_FAILED back to RUN_IN_PROGRESS.

 ## Preconditions

 - Run must be in RUN_FAILED phase
 - TERMINATED runs cannot be recovered (their saved state may be incomplete)
 - CANCELLED runs cannot be recovered (intentional user action)
 - User must have can_edit permission on the run

 ## Idempotency

 If recovery is already in progress (run moved to IN_PROGRESS after
 a previous recover call), the call succeeds as a no-op and returns current state.

 ## Use Cases

 - Agent failed due to transient error (network timeout, rate limit)
 - External API was down but is now available
 - Bug was fixed and agent should continue from failure point
 - Retry after investigating and fixing the root cause

 ## Example

 {
   "id": "run_abc123xyz456"
 }

fields.name: Id
fields.description:
Run ID to recover.

 Must be in FAILED phase. TERMINATED and CANCELLED runs
 cannot be recovered.

 Format: "run_{ulid}" (auto-generated unique identifier)
 Example: "run_abc123xyz456"

 Validation: Required, cannot be empty

methodTypes.name: PauseRunInput
methodTypes.description:
PauseRunInput requests temporarily pausing a run.

 Pauses the agent where it is. Unlike an interrupt, the run is NOT terminal:
 it reads RUN_PAUSED, uses no resources while paused, and the resume RPC
 continues it from where it left off.

 ## Preconditions

 - Run must be in RUN_PENDING or RUN_IN_PROGRESS phase
 - Cannot pause already paused or terminal runs

 ## Use Cases

 - User wants to review agent progress before continuing
 - Scheduled maintenance window requires pausing work
 - Rate limit concerns require throttling agent work
 - Need to modify agent configuration before continuing

 ## Example

 {
   "id": "run_abc123xyz456",
   "reason": "Pausing to review progress before continuing"
 }

fields.name: Id
fields.description:
Run ID to pause.

 Must be in PENDING or IN_PROGRESS phase. Cannot pause
 runs that are already terminal (COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, TERMINATED).

 Format: "run_{ulid}" (auto-generated unique identifier)
 Example: "run_abc123xyz456"

 Validation: Required, cannot be empty

fields.name: Reason
fields.description:
Human-readable reason for pausing.

 Stored in the audit trail for operational debugging and compliance.
 Helps track why the pause was needed.

 Examples:
 - "Pausing for scheduled maintenance window"
 - "User requested pause to review progress"
 - "Pausing due to rate limit concerns"
 - "Emergency pause - investigating issue"

methodTypes.name: ResumeRunInput
methodTypes.description:
ResumeRunInput requests resuming a paused run.

 Continues the run from where it was paused; the run moves back to
 RUN_IN_PROGRESS. How a turn's state is saved is the harness's
 ([Harnesses](/docs/concepts/harnesses)).

 ## Preconditions

 - Run must be in RUN_PAUSED phase
 - Cannot resume non-paused runs

 ## Idempotency

 If the run is not paused (already IN_PROGRESS),
 the call succeeds as a no-op and returns the current run state.

 ## Example

 {
   "id": "run_abc123xyz456"
 }

   "id": "run_abc123xyz456"
 }

Run ID to resume.

 Must be in PAUSED phase. Cannot resume runs
 that are not paused.

 Format: "run_{ulid}" (auto-generated unique identifier)
 Example: "run_abc123xyz456"

 Validation: Required, cannot be empty

methodTypes.name: GetArtifactDownloadUrlRequest
methodTypes.description:
GetArtifactDownloadUrlRequest requests a download URL for a run's stored
 content.

 This endpoint generates a presigned URL for one object the run's runner
 stored. The URL is time-limited and can be used for direct HTTP download
 without authentication.

 ## Authorization

 Requires can_view permission on the run. This ensures users can only
 access stored content from runs they have access to.

 ## Security

 The storage_key is validated to ensure it belongs to the specified run.
 Storage keys must start with "artifacts/{run_id}/" to prevent path
 traversal attacks where a user could request URLs for another run's
 content.

 ## Use Cases

 - Web UI downloading a tool call's full output
 - Refreshing expired download URLs

 ## Example

 Request:
 {
   "run_id": "run_abc123xyz456",
   "storage_key": "artifacts/run_abc123xyz456/toolcalls/call_01.txt"
 }

 Response:
 {
   "download_url": "https://r2.example.com/...",
   "expires_at": "2026-02-20T10:30:00Z"
 }

fields.name: RunId
fields.description:
ID of the run that stored the content.

 Used for authorization (can_view check) and storage_key validation.

 Format: "run_{ulid}"
 Example: "run_abc123xyz456"

 Validation: Required, minimum 1 character

fields.name: StorageKey
fields.description:
Storage key of the content to download.

 Must be content of the specified run. The storage_key is validated
 to start with "artifacts/{run_id}/" to prevent access to another
 run's content.

 Obtain this value from a ToolCallOutputRef.storage_key the run recorded.

 Format: "artifacts/{run_id}/{path}"
 Example: "artifacts/run_abc123xyz456/toolcalls/call_01.txt"

 Validation: Required, minimum 1 character

fields.name: AsAttachment
fields.description: Whether the URL should force a browser download instead of inline display. When true, the presigned URL carries a Content-Disposition: attachment header keyed to the stored object's name, so a browser navigating to it saves the file rather than rendering it in a tab. Browsers ignore the HTML `download` attribute on cross-origin URLs (e.g. presigned R2), so the disposition MUST be signed into the URL itself — this flag is how a caller requests it. When false (the default), the URL displays inline. Inline is required for rendering surfaces such as an `` pointing at an offloaded screenshot; forcing a download there would break the render. Use true for click-to-download affordances; false (or unset) for inline rendering and programmatic reads.

methodTypes.name: GetArtifactDownloadUrlResponse
methodTypes.description:
GetArtifactDownloadUrlResponse returns a presigned download URL for a
 run's stored content.

 The download_url can be used with a simple HTTP GET request to download
 the content. No authentication headers are required - the URL contains
 embedded authorization.

fields.name: DownloadUrl
fields.description:
Presigned URL for downloading the content.

 Valid for direct HTTP GET request without authentication.
 The URL includes embedded authorization that expires at expires_at.

 Example: "https://r2.cloudflarestorage.com/bucket/artifacts/...?X-Amz-Signature=..."
 With local storage the URL is the server's own file server, signed
 by the server: "http://localhost:7235/artifacts/...?exp=...&sig=..."

fields.name: ExpiresAt
fields.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the download URL expires.

 After this time, the URL will no longer work and a new URL
 must be requested via this endpoint.

 Default expiration: 7 days from generation.

 Example: "2026-02-20T10:30:00Z"

methodTypes.name: GetArtifactContentRequest
methodTypes.description:
GetArtifactContentRequest reads the raw bytes of a run's stored content.

 Unlike getArtifactDownloadUrl (which returns a presigned URL for direct
 browser download), this endpoint returns the bytes through the Stigmer
 API. This eliminates CORS concerns for SDK consumers who need to read
 the content programmatically — e.g., for in-app preview rendering.

 ## Authorization

 Requires can_view permission on the run. This ensures users can only
 read stored content from runs they have access to.

 ## Security

 The storage_key is validated to ensure it belongs to the specified run.
 Storage keys must start with "artifacts/{run_id}/" to prevent path
 traversal attacks where a user could request another run's content.

 ## Size Limit

 The server enforces a maximum content size (default: 512 KB). If the
 content exceeds max_bytes, the response contains the first max_bytes of
 it with truncated=true. Callers can use total_size_bytes to decide
 whether to offer a full download via getArtifactDownloadUrl instead.

 ## Use Cases

 - Web UI showing a tool call's offloaded output
 - Web UI showing a changed file's diff or content in file review

 ## Example

 Request:
 {
   "run_id": "run_abc123xyz456",
   "storage_key": "artifacts/run_abc123xyz456/toolcalls/call_01.txt"
 }

 Response:
 {
   "content": <bytes>,
   "content_type": "text/plain",
   "total_size_bytes": 1842,
   "truncated": false
 }

fields.name: RunId
fields.description:
ID of the run that stored the content.

 Used for authorization (can_view check) and storage_key validation.

 Format: "run_{ulid}"
 Example: "run_abc123xyz456"

 Validation: Required, minimum 1 character

fields.name: StorageKey
fields.description:
Storage key of the content to read.

 Must be content of the specified run. The storage_key is validated
 to start with "artifacts/{run_id}/" to prevent access to another
 run's content.

 Obtain this value from a ToolCallOutputRef.storage_key the run recorded.

 Format: "artifacts/{run_id}/{path}"
 Example: "artifacts/run_abc123xyz456/toolcalls/call_01.txt"

 Validation: Required, minimum 1 character

fields.name: MaxBytes
fields.description:
Maximum number of bytes to return.

 If the content is larger than this limit, the response will contain
 the first max_bytes of it with truncated=true.

 When 0 or unset, the server applies a default limit (512 KB).
 The server may also enforce a hard upper bound regardless of this value.

 Example: 524288 (512 KB)

fields.name: EntryPath
fields.description:
For stored ZIP content: extract a specific entry by its path within
 the archive instead of returning the raw ZIP bytes.

 When empty, returns the full content (existing behavior).
 When the stored object is not a ZIP, this field is ignored.

 The path must match an entry in the archive exactly (case-sensitive).
 List the archive's entries to discover valid values.

 Example: "SKILL.md", "scripts/init_skill.py"

methodTypes.name: GetArtifactContentResponse
methodTypes.description:
GetArtifactContentResponse returns the raw bytes of a run's stored
 content.

 The content field contains the bytes (up to max_bytes). For text,
 clients decode via TextDecoder or equivalent. The content_type field
 provides a hint for rendering (detected by file extension).

fields.name: Content
fields.description:
Raw content (up to max_bytes).

 For text (YAML, JSON, Markdown, etc.), decode as UTF-8.
 For binary content, this contains raw bytes — but callers should
 generally use getArtifactDownloadUrl for binary downloads instead.

fields.name: ContentType
fields.description:
Detected content type based on file extension.

 Examples: "text/yaml", "text/plain", "application/json",
 "application/zip".

 This is a best-effort detection — not based on content inspection.

fields.name: TotalSizeBytes
fields.description:
Actual total size of the content in bytes.

 May be larger than len(content) when truncated=true.
 Callers can use this to show "showing 512 KB of 2.1 MB" messages
 or to decide whether to offer a full download link.

fields.name: Truncated
fields.description:
Whether the content was truncated to fit within max_bytes.

 When true, content contains only the first max_bytes of it.
 The full content can be downloaded via getArtifactDownloadUrl.

GetRunSummaryRequest fetches aggregated run statistics

Time window for aggregation.

methodTypes.name: RunSummary
methodTypes.description:
RunSummary contains aggregated operational statistics for agent
 runs. Designed for the platform dashboard's unified health view.

 Tokens are intentionally omitted. The dashboard reads them from
 getOrgUsageReport, so usage is never counted from two places.

fields.name: ActiveCount
fields.description:
Number of runs currently in a non-terminal phase
 (PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL, PAUSED).

fields.name: PhaseCounts
fields.description:
Run counts broken down by RunPhase enum value.

 Keys are RunPhase enum values (as int32).
 Only phases with at least one run are included.

Mean run duration (from started_at to completed_at) for completed

 Zero when no completed runs exist.

fields.name: TopFailingAgents
