Agents with the highest failure count in the time window, ranked descending.

 Capped at 10 entries.

enumTypes.name: RunControlSignal
enumTypes.description:
RunControlSignal is a platform-to-runner directive returned by the
 updateStatus RPC. The runner inspects this signal after every status
 update and acts accordingly.

 Signal sources are opaque to the runner — the platform may set STOP due
 to an admin kill, a user-configured budget cap, or any other enforcement
 mechanism. The runner does not know or care about the source; it only
 reacts to the signal value.

values.name: RUN_CONTROL_SIGNAL_STOP
values.description:
Run must stop gracefully. The runner should block further tool
 calls and give the model one final turn to produce a summary.

values.name: RUN_CONTROL_SIGNAL_WARNING
values.description:
Informational warning (e.g. a budget cap nearly reached). The runner
 logs the warning and continues the run.

enumTypes.name: RunPhase
enumTypes.description:
RunPhase defines the lifecycle phase of a run.

 Phase Transitions:

 Normal flow:
 RUN_PENDING → RUN_IN_PROGRESS → RUN_COMPLETED

 Failure flow:
 RUN_PENDING → RUN_IN_PROGRESS → RUN_FAILED

 Termination flow (platform-initiated stop):
 RUN_IN_PROGRESS → RUN_TERMINATED

 Approval flow (HITL):
 RUN_IN_PROGRESS → RUN_WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL → RUN_IN_PROGRESS

 Pause/Resume flow:
 RUN_IN_PROGRESS → RUN_PAUSED → RUN_IN_PROGRESS

 Terminal States:
 - RUN_COMPLETED: Agent finished successfully
 - RUN_FAILED: Agent encountered an unexpected error
 - RUN_TERMINATED: Platform stopped the agent (stall, budget, or force-kill)
 - RUN_CANCELLED: User gracefully stopped the agent

 Non-Terminal States:
 - RUN_WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL: Awaiting user approval for tool
 - RUN_PAUSED: Temporarily paused, can be resumed

values.name: RUN_PENDING
values.description: Run is queued and waiting for a worker to start processing.

values.name: RUN_IN_PROGRESS
values.description: Run is in progress — the agent is processing and producing output.

values.name: RUN_COMPLETED
values.description: Run finished successfully and the agent produced a final response.

values.name: RUN_FAILED
values.description: Run encountered an unexpected error and could not finish.

values.name: RUN_CANCELLED
values.description: Run was gracefully stopped by the user before it finished.

values.name: RUN_TERMINATED
values.description:
Run was stopped by the platform.

 Unlike CANCELLED (user-initiated graceful stop) and FAILED (unexpected
 error), TERMINATED means the platform intentionally stopped this
 run — either via automated safety mechanisms or user-initiated
 force-kill.

 Terminal state — run will not change phases again.

 When this phase is reached:
 - completed_at timestamp is set
 - error field contains the termination reason

 Use Cases:
 - Agent stalled — no events for the configured timeout; the session
   continues with a follow-up message
 - Agent exhausted its tool-call budget; the session continues with a
   follow-up message
 - Force-stop stuck agents that don't respond to cancellation (the
   Terminate RPC)
 - Kill agents consuming excessive resources

 Terminated vs Cancelled vs Failed:
 - Terminated: Platform stopped it (automated or force-kill)
 - Cancelled: User gracefully stopped it (the turn ended cleanly)
 - Failed: Something broke unexpectedly (exception, crash)

values.name: RUN_WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL
values.description:
Blocked on tool approval.

 The agent has encountered a tool that requires a person's answer before
 it runs. The waiting call is the session's agent.tool_use event with
 evaluated_permission ask, and SessionCommandController.confirmToolUse or
 grantPermission answers it.

 This is NOT a terminal state: the run returns to RUN_IN_PROGRESS once
 every waiting call is answered. A denied call does not fail the run; the
 model reads the denial and adapts. To stop the whole turn, interrupt the
 session.

values.name: RUN_PAUSED
values.description:
Run was paused by user and can be resumed.

 The run was temporarily stopped and can continue from where it left
 off. Unlike CANCELLED, the run is not terminal.

 Pause flow:
 RUN_IN_PROGRESS → RUN_PAUSED

 Resume flow:
 RUN_PAUSED → RUN_IN_PROGRESS

 NOT a terminal state - run can be resumed.

 When this phase is reached:
 - No completed_at timestamp (run is not finished)
 - The resume RPC continues the run from where it was paused

enumTypes.name: RunSummaryTimeWindow
enumTypes.description: Controls the time range for run summary queries.

enumTypes.name: ApprovalMode
enumTypes.description:
ApprovalMode controls how a run resolves HITL approval gates.

 The approval default (shell commands, file writes and deletes, and MCP tools
 their server marks destructive) decides WHICH tools are gated; this mode
 decides WHAT HAPPENS when a gate fires. It exists for lanes where no
 approver is present at the conversation — a routine's fire, Slack and
 WhatsApp channels, and chat links' guests — where an interactive pause
 would park the run in RUN_WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL forever.

 The mode is a fact of the lane the run came through, recorded by
 the server on RunStatus.approval_mode, never chosen by the
 request or the external user: it is runtime policy owned by the lane,
 exactly like the bounded execution profile. Every other turn (console,
 CLI) is INTERACTIVE.

 Two different consents, deliberately separated:
 - Operator consent (this gate) protects the org's tools and data and is
   never delegated to an external user — a channel guest cannot authorize
   the org's destructive operations.
 - End-user intent confirmation ("book Monday 10 AM — shall I?") is
   conversational, owned by the agent's instructions.

values.name: APPROVAL_MODE_INTERACTIVE
values.description:
Interactive approval (today's behavior): a gated tool pauses the
 run (RUN_WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL) until a person answers it through
 SessionCommandController.confirmToolUse or grantPermission. No timeout — the run waits
 indefinitely.

values.name: APPROVAL_MODE_UNATTENDED
values.description:
Unattended: no approver exists where the run came from (a routine, a
 channel). A gated tool is
 resolved as an automatic SKIP — the tool does NOT run, the model is told
 the action requires an approval that is not available in this
 conversation and to adapt and explain in plain language, and the turn
 continues to normal completion. The skipped call is stamped
 TOOL_CALL_SKIPPED with approval_policy_source = UNATTENDED_SKIP; no
 approval-request event is authored (nothing is ever pending).

 A future "park the turn and notify an org approver asynchronously"
 behavior will be a NEW enum value, not a reinterpretation of this one.

enumTypes.name: ApiResourceKind
enumTypes.description: API resource kinds for Stigmer.

values.name: api_resource_version
values.description: Immutable version record tracking changes to an API resource.

values.name: grant
values.description:
One role given to one principal on one resource. Who holds what on a
 resource is the set of its grants.

values.name: identity_account
values.description: User account in the identity system.

values.name: api_key
values.description: Credential for programmatic API access.

values.name: invitation
values.description: Shareable link for joining an organization with a configurable role.

values.name: federation_issuer
values.description:
An outside issuer whose tokens Stigmer accepts for its own users
 (identity federation): its keys, its audience, and what its tokens get.

values.name: oauth_app
values.description: Registered OAuth application with an external vendor for outbound authentication.

values.name: team
values.description: Named group of an organization's people that access is shared with as one.

values.name: organization
values.description:
The boundary that holds people, Agents, Sessions and secrets
 together; nothing outside it sees them.

 Its id is a minted org_<ulid> that never changes; every organization-scoped
 resource names it by that id (metadata.org). Its slug is unique across the
 server and may change through rename; requests may name the organization
 by either.

values.name: platform
values.description: Singleton platform instance representing the Stigmer deployment.

values.name: agent
values.description: AI assistant with instructions, tools, skills, and a delegation model.

values.name: run
values.description: Single run of an agent within a session, tracking tool calls and responses.

values.name: session
values.description: Conversation thread between a user and an agent.

values.name: skill
values.description: Knowledge resource that provides domain-specific context to an agent.

values.name: channel
values.description:
A way people reach an agent: a chat link or website widget, a Slack
 workspace, or a WhatsApp number.

values.name: channel_app
values.description:
Customer-owned messaging-platform app (e.g. a Slack app) that
 channels can install through instead of the shared platform app.

values.name: routine
values.description:
A saved agent invocation, run on an optional schedule or fired by Run now
 or over the API, acting as its owner.

values.name: memory
values.description: Agent-proposed, user-confirmed fact the platform remembers about a person.

values.name: plugin
values.description:
An installed Agent Plugins package: one thing holding skills, agents,
 hooks and MCP servers, which agents and conversations list whole.

values.name: vault
values.description:
A person's or an organization's box of logins (matched by a tool's
 address) and secrets (matched by name) that runs use.

values.name: score
values.description:
One grade of a finished run: a person's thumbs or a free run-health
 check.

values.name: scoring_rule
values.description:
AI grading switched on for one agent: its sample rate, monthly spending
 limit and judge model.

values.name: eval_run
values.description:
One run of test cases on an agent, or on a plugin on the built-in
 assistant, optionally with and without a plugin.

values.name: eval
values.description:
A set of test cases for an agent: an evals/ folder in Claude Code's
 plugin-eval format, pushed whole.

values.name: environment
values.description:
A named sandbox setup: the packages installed in every sandbox a
 conversation using it runs in, and the hosts it may reach.

values.name: file
values.description:
A file uploaded once and named by its id: given to a conversation with
 a message, held in a conversation's resources, or kept by its uploader.

values.name: plan
values.description:
Catalog entry naming a bundle of entitlements and the terms that buy it.

 Platform-level: a plan belongs to no organization, so it carries no
 authorization scope and no owner. Immutable once created; a change of
 terms is a new Plan and the old one retires.

values.name: subscription
values.description:
An organization's binding to a Plan; at most one active per organization.

 System-created: the payment system drives its lifecycle, so it has no
 owner and grants no roles. Its reads and writes authorize on the
 organization through the billing permissions.

values.name: license
values.description:
A signed grant of entitlements to a self-hosting customer for a term.

 Platform-level: issued by the cloud's operators and verified offline by
 the Enterprise server, so the customer is a value inside the license
 (which may or may not name a cloud organization) and the kind has no
 authorization scope and no owner. Claims are immutable once signed; a
 renewal is a new License.

enumTypes.name: FileChangeKind
enumTypes.description:
FileChangeKind is the per-file outcome within a FileChangeSet.

 The minimal set that covers the overwhelming majority of edits; COPY /
 MODE_CHANGE / SYMLINK_CHANGE are deferred (adding enum values later is
 non-breaking).

values.name: FILE_CHANGE_KIND_ADD
values.description: A new file was created.

values.name: FILE_CHANGE_KIND_MODIFY
values.description: An existing file's contents changed.

values.name: FILE_CHANGE_KIND_DELETE
values.description: A file was deleted.

values.name: FILE_CHANGE_KIND_RENAME
values.description:
A file was renamed or moved; path_before holds the source, path_after the
 destination.

values.name: FILE_CHANGE_KIND_BINARY_CHANGE
values.description:
A binary file changed; rendered as "binary file changed" rather than a text
 diff.

enumTypes.name: FileCaptureClass
enumTypes.description:
FileCaptureClass records how a file was captured, which governs which
 substrate (git tree ref vs CAS) holds its bytes and whether it is reviewable
 before CAS lands.

values.name: FILE_CAPTURE_CLASS_GIT_TRACKED
values.description: A git-tracked file; captured via the git no-commit tree snapshot.

values.name: FILE_CAPTURE_CLASS_GIT_UNTRACKED_CAPTURED
values.description: A git-untracked (but not ignored) file captured into the snapshot.

values.name: FILE_CAPTURE_CLASS_GIT_IGNORED_CAPTURED
values.description: A gitignored file captured via CAS.

values.name: FILE_CAPTURE_CLASS_NON_GIT_CAS
values.description: A file in a non-git workspace captured via CAS.

enumTypes.name: FileReviewBlockReason
enumTypes.description:
FileReviewBlockReason is the honest cause a captured file's diff is not fully
 reviewable (carried on CapturedFileChange.blocked_reason, set only when
 diff_complete == false). It is INFORMATIONAL provenance for the review UI —
 never an enforcement input and never folded into file_digest/aggregate_digest.
 Binary changes are conveyed by FileContent.is_binary, not here, so there is no
 BINARY value (it would duplicate a signal the wire already carries).

values.name: FILE_REVIEW_BLOCK_REASON_SECRET_WITHHELD
values.description:
A secret-like path: the bytes were deliberately never
 captured, so there is nothing to review. Authored content-less by the runner.

values.name: FILE_REVIEW_BLOCK_REASON_SIZE_ELIDED
values.description:
Captured, then its inline bodies were dropped to keep the persisted status
 under its size limit. The content exists but is not inline for review.

values.name: FILE_REVIEW_BLOCK_REASON_UNREVIEWABLE
values.description:
Generic non-capturable cause (forward-compat catch-all; e.g. a future
 non-git path class). Mirrors the fail-open spirit of DIFF_UNREVIEWABLE.

enumTypes.name: DiffCompleteness
enumTypes.description:
DiffCompleteness describes whether a change set's rendered diff is complete
 enough to approve safely. A non-COMPLETE value blocks normal approval so an
 elided or binary-only diff can never be approved as if it were the whole
 change. The value is a rollup the runner derives from the per-file
 diff_complete + is_binary signals; it is an honest UI/audit signal, never the
 enforcement boundary — the backend gate always re-derives the keep-all
 condition from the per-file changes so a stale or mislabeled rollup can never
 widen what may be approved.

values.name: DIFF_COMPLETENESS_COMPLETE
values.description: Every file's full diff is available; safe to approve.

values.name: DIFF_COMPLETENESS_PARTIAL_BLOCKED
values.description:
At least one file has a non-binary incompleteness (elided/truncated/
 secret-withheld/uncapturable) with no keepable bytes. The set cannot be
 approved in one shot; it is resolved per file (keep the reviewable files,
 discard the rest).

values.name: DIFF_COMPLETENESS_BINARY_SUMMARY_ONLY
values.description:
The set's ONLY incompleteness is binary files: every non-binary file is
 fully reviewable, and the remaining files are binary (a byte-true summary,
 no text diff). Includes mixed sets (e.g. text edits + generated images).
 Such a set can be kept in one action via a CHANGE_SET-scoped APPROVE
 carrying acknowledge_unreviewable=true ("Keep all"). The acknowledgment
 relaxes completeness only — never the expected_digest gate ("what you
 approve is what gets applied").

enumTypes.name: ServiceTier
enumTypes.description:
ServiceTier selects the provider-side speed/service tier for a run's
 model calls.

 Providers spell this differently — Cursor exposes per-model "fast" variants
 at higher per-token rates, Anthropic and OpenAI expose service tiers — but
 the platform semantic is uniform: the tier is a deterministic, user-selected
 attribute validated against the model registry at create time. A tier is
 selectable for a model only when the registry prices it
 (pricingVariants.<tier>), so a selected tier is always billable.

 The load-bearing rule: UNSPECIFIED resolves to SERVICE_TIER_STANDARD — never
 the provider account default. The runner always sends the provider an
 explicit variant selection, so an out-of-band account setting can never
 silently change what a run pays (stigmer/stigmer#357).

values.name: SERVICE_TIER_STANDARD
values.description:
Standard tier: the model's base-priced configuration, requested
 explicitly.

values.name: SERVICE_TIER_FAST
values.description:
Fast tier: the model's fast variant, billed at the registry's fast
 variant rates.

 Valid only for models whose registry entry declares a fast pricing
 variant; refused at run create otherwise.

enumTypes.name: ThinkingMode
enumTypes.description:
ThinkingMode selects the model's extended-reasoning ("thinking") variant
 for a run's model calls — the second variant dimension alongside
 ServiceTier (stigmer/stigmer#772).

 Unlike the fast tier, thinking is NOT a separately priced dimension:
 Cursor bills thinking variants at the model's base per-token rates
 (verified against the live pricing page and 277 team-ledger events on
 2026-08-15 — thinking wire ids bill exactly base; thinking+fast bills
 exactly the fast variant rate). Thinking costs more only by generating
 additional reasoning tokens, billed as ordinary output. Selectability is
 therefore CAPABILITY-gated, not pricing-gated: ENABLED is valid only for
 models whose registry entry on the run's harness declares a
 thinking capability (capabilities.thinking or capabilities.adaptive_thinking),
 refused at create time otherwise. ENABLED means "the model reasons before
 it answers", in the form its entry declares: a fixed budget or adaptive
 depth.

 The load-bearing rule mirrors ServiceTier: UNSPECIFIED resolves to
 THINKING_MODE_DISABLED — never the provider account default. Several
 catalog default variants are thinking=true (claude-haiku-4-5), so an
 unpinned selection would silently follow an out-of-band account setting;
 the runner always sends an explicit thinking pin where the model declares
 the parameter. The one exception is a model whose entry declares
 capabilities.thinking_required: it always thinks, so an explicit DISABLED
 is refused at create and UNSPECIFIED runs with thinking on.

values.name: THINKING_MODE_DISABLED
values.description:
Extended reasoning off: the model's base variant, requested explicitly
 (thinking=false pinned where the model declares the parameter).
 Refused at run create for a model that requires thinking.

values.name: THINKING_MODE_ENABLED
values.description:
Extended reasoning on: the model's thinking variant, billed at base
 per-token rates (reasoning tokens bill as output tokens).

 Valid only for models whose registry entry on the run's harness
 declares a thinking capability; refused at run create otherwise.

enumTypes.name: RunValueDeclarerKind
enumTypes.description: Who declared a value a turn uses.

values.name: RUN_VALUE_DECLARER_KIND_AGENT
values.description: The turn's agent, in its env.

values.name: RUN_VALUE_DECLARER_KIND_TOOL
values.description: A tool (an MCP server) the turn uses, in its env or its login.

values.name: RUN_VALUE_DECLARER_KIND_REPOSITORY
values.description: A repository the turn clones, for its token.

values.name: RUN_VALUE_DECLARER_KIND_PLUGIN
values.description: A plugin the turn uses, for its hooks.

values.name: RUN_VALUE_DECLARER_KIND_SUBAGENT
values.description: A saved agent the turn's agent lists as a subagent, in its env.

enumTypes.name: RunValueOrigin
enumTypes.description: Where a value a turn uses lives.

values.name: RUN_VALUE_ORIGIN_REPOSITORY_TOKEN
values.description: The conversation's own token for the repository.

values.name: RUN_VALUE_ORIGIN_MY_VAULT
values.description: The turn's person's My vault.

values.name: RUN_VALUE_ORIGIN_VAULT
values.description: A vault the conversation lists.

values.name: RUN_VALUE_ORIGIN_SURFACE_VAULT
values.description:
A vault of the routine, channel or embedding settings a turn with no
 person came through. The value's name is older than this wording and
 stays: an enum value is a wire identifier.

values.name: RUN_VALUE_ORIGIN_DECLARATION
values.description: The declaration's own plain default.

enumTypes.name: SnapshotKind
enumTypes.description: SnapshotKind is the substrate backing a SnapshotRef.

values.name: SNAPSHOT_KIND_GIT_TREE_REF
values.description: A git no-commit tree ref (git-tracked/untracked paths only).

values.name: SNAPSHOT_KIND_CAS_MANIFEST
values.description: A content-addressed manifest (ignored/non-git paths).

values.name: SNAPSHOT_KIND_HYBRID
values.description: Both a git tree ref and a CAS manifest (mixed workspace).

enumTypes.name: WorkspaceWriteBackPhase
enumTypes.description:
WorkspaceWriteBackPhase tracks the progress of a single workspace
 write-back through its lifecycle steps.

 The phases are ordered: COMMITTED -> PUSHED -> PR_CREATED.
 FAILED can be reached from any step.

values.name: WORKSPACE_WRITE_BACK_COMMITTED
values.description: Changes were committed to a new branch in the sandbox.

values.name: WORKSPACE_WRITE_BACK_PUSHED
values.description: The branch was pushed to the remote repository.

values.name: WORKSPACE_WRITE_BACK_PR_CREATED
values.description: A pull request was created on the remote repository.

values.name: WORKSPACE_WRITE_BACK_FAILED
values.description: The write-back failed at some step. Check the error field.

enumTypes.name: ApiResourceVisibility
enumTypes.description:
Visibility controls who can access an API resource.
 This is orthogonal to ownership - visibility is about access control,
 while ownership (org) determines who manages the resource.

 Key distinction:
 - Ownership: Which organization controls/manages the resource
 - Visibility: Who can access/use the resource

 All resources belong to an organization. Visibility determines which
 users, inside that organization or in its child organizations, can read
 the resource. No level reaches every
 account on the server.

 The visibility levels map to FGA tuples:
 - PRIVATE: no additional viewer tuples (owner-only access)
 - ORG: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer tuple (everyone in the
   org — the org role hierarchy flows downward, so owners, admins, members
   AND read-only viewers all satisfy the organization#viewer userset)
 - CHILD_ORGS: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer
   (everyone in every child organization of the owning organization)
 - PUBLIC: retired; see the value's own comment.

values.name: visibility_private
values.description:
Only the owner, explicitly granted principals, and — for blueprint kinds
 in the cloud edition — org admins can access.
 This is the default for personal and run-scoped resources.

 Org admins count as owners of blueprint kinds (agent, channel,
 skill, plugin), so a private blueprint stays
 manageable — and visible — to its org's admins. Personal kinds
 (sessions) stay creator-only.

values.name: visibility_public
values.description:
Retired. This level made a resource readable to every account on the
 server; it is refused at create and at updateVisibility for every kind,
 and every stored row that held it has been moved to visibility_org.
 Sharing across organizations happens through plugins (a copy is
 installed and owned) or, from a parent organization to its children,
 through visibility_child_orgs.

values.name: visibility_org
values.description:
Everyone in the owning organization can access (read) this resource —
 all org roles including read-only viewers (the role just-in-time provisioning
 grants by default). Running or otherwise spending against the resource
 still requires the org-level member-or-guest permissions
 (can_create_session / can_create_run_in); org visibility widens
 read, never spend.

 FGA tuple: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer
 (The tuple once targeted organization#member, which
 excluded viewer-role users; the authorization model no longer admits
 that shape.)

values.name: visibility_child_orgs
values.description:
Everyone in every child organization of the owning organization can
 read and run this resource: the shared catalog an organization offers
 the organizations under it (spec.parent_org). Child organizations
 created later gain access automatically, and no other organization
 does. Instances, sessions, runs and vaults are never shared
 this way: each child runs the shared blueprint inside its own boundary.

 Only valid for blueprint kinds with supports_child_orgs: true, and only
 in an organization that is not itself a child.

 FGA tuple: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer

enumTypes.name: InteractionMode
enumTypes.description:
InteractionMode controls the agent's behavioral posture for a run.

 Determines what the agent is allowed to do — analysis only, or full
 read-write access. Mode is set per message
 (RunSpec.interaction_mode) and does not carry over between
 runs.

 Enforcement:
 - Native harness: tool-level enforcement — write tools are
   removed from the tool set in PLAN mode.
 - Cursor harness: best-effort via system prompt injection. The Cursor SDK
   does not expose a mode parameter, so the agent is instructed not to
   make changes. When the SDK adds native mode support, the prompt-based
   approach will be replaced.

values.name: INTERACTION_MODE_AGENT
values.description:
Full agent mode with unrestricted tool access.

 The agent can read, write, create, edit, and delete files; run shell
 commands; and invoke any configured tool. This is the standard
 execution mode for interactive sessions.

values.name: INTERACTION_MODE_PLAN
values.description:
Read-only planning mode — analysis and recommendations only.

 The agent can read files, search code, list directories, and reason
 about the codebase, but cannot create, edit, or delete files or run
 mutating shell commands. Designed for exploring approaches, producing
 implementation plans, and answering architectural questions without
 side effects.

 Native harness: enforced by removing write tools from the tool set.
 Cursor harness: best-effort via system prompt directive.

enumTypes.name: Harness
enumTypes.description:
Harness identifies the execution engine that processes agent activities
 for a session.

 Each harness corresponds to a different Temporal activity type registered
 by the runner daemon. The harness determines:
 - Which tools the agent has access to
 - How conversation state is managed (Stigmer checkpoints vs engine-native)
 - Which LLM models are available
 - Billing tier and cost structure

 HARNESS_UNSPECIFIED defaults to HARNESS_NATIVE for backward compatibility.

values.name: HARNESS_NATIVE
values.description:
Stigmer's native execution engine.

 Stigmer-managed checkpoints, custom tools, sandbox isolation,
 pause/resume, and full HITL approval flow.

values.name: HARNESS_CURSOR
values.description:
Cursor SDK execution engine.

 Cursor-managed conversation state, Cursor built-in tools + MCP,
 both local and cloud runtimes. Premium billing tier.

enumTypes.name: CursorMode
enumTypes.description:
CursorMode selects the Cursor SDK agent type for sessions using
 HARNESS_CURSOR.

 Determined once at session creation and never changed mid-session.
 Switching would lose Cursor-side conversation state because local
 agents (agent- prefix) and cloud agents (bc- prefix) maintain
 separate, incompatible conversation stores.

 Ignored when harness is not HARNESS_CURSOR.

values.name: CURSOR_MODE_LOCAL
values.description:
Local Cursor agent created with a local cwd configuration.

 Works with any workspace source (git or local path). Conversation
 state is carried by the Cursor SDK's native local store, which the
 runner persists on the durable workspace volume so Agent.resume()
 survives pod restart and snapshot restore.

values.name: CURSOR_MODE_CLOUD
values.description:
Cloud Cursor agent created with a cloud repos configuration.

 Requires every resource to be a git repository (HTTPS URL).
 Cursor natively manages conversation state for cloud agents.
 Feature-flagged — requires STIGMER_CURSOR_CLOUD_MODE_ENABLED.

enumTypes.name: ExecutionTarget
enumTypes.description:
ExecutionTarget specifies where session activities are executed.

 Determines whether the runner that processes agent activities lives on the
 client's machine (desktop app or CLI) or in a cloud-provisioned sandbox.
 Set at session creation time and immutable once a run has started —
 workspace state may not be portable between local and cloud environments.

values.name: EXECUTION_TARGET_LOCAL
values.description:
Client's embedded runner handles activities.

 Desktop app or CLI spawns a local runner process that polls the
 session's task queue. No server-side provisioning needed.

values.name: EXECUTION_TARGET_CLOUD
values.description:
Server provisions a cloud sandbox for execution.

 The control plane triggers EnsureSessionSandbox to create an isolated
 environment with a runner polling the session's task queue.

enumTypes.name: GitWriteBackMode
enumTypes.description: GitWriteBackMode controls the platform's git workflow for a git-backed workspace entry.

values.name: GIT_WRITE_BACK_BRANCH_AND_PR
values.description: Create a branch and pull request from the agent's file changes after the run completes.

enumTypes.name: EvalMockKind
enumTypes.description: EvalMockKind is how a mocked tool answers.

values.name: eval_mock_kind_fixed
values.description: The mock file's body, with its substitutions.

values.name: eval_mock_kind_agent
values.description: A model acting as the server from the mock file's instructions.

enumTypes.name: ProviderKeySource
enumTypes.description:
Whose provider credential served a proxied LLM call.

 The proxy picks the key, injects it upstream, and reports the same source
 with the usage payload, so the record never disagrees with what was sent
 on the wire.

values.name: PROVIDER_KEY_SOURCE_PLATFORM
values.description: A connection the platform provides served the call.

values.name: PROVIDER_KEY_SOURCE_ORGANIZATION
values.description:
The organization's own provider key served the call (bring-your-own
 provider keys): the provider bills the organization directly.

resourceDescription:
Run represents a single run instance (conversational).
 Follows the standard pattern: spec contains user inputs, status contains run results.

statusType.name: RunStatus
statusType.description:
RunStatus contains all run results and state.
 Everything populated during or after the run goes here, not in spec.
 The conversation itself (messages, tool calls, approvals, todos,
 subagents, structured output and file-review decisions) is the session's
 event log (SessionEvent), not a field here.

fields.name: Audit
fields.description: Standard audit information (created_at, updated_at, created_by, etc.)

fields.name: Phase
fields.description:
Current run lifecycle phase.
 Tracks the run state from creation (PENDING) through active processing (IN_PROGRESS)
 to terminal states (COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED).

fields.name: Error
fields.description:
Error message if the run failed.
 Only populated when phase == RUN_FAILED.

fields.name: StartedAt
fields.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the run started.
 Example: "2025-01-10T10:30:00Z"

fields.name: CompletedAt
fields.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the run completed, failed, or was cancelled.
 Only populated for terminal states.

fields.name: WorkspaceWriteBacks
fields.description:
Git write-back outcomes for workspace entries that had changes.

 One entry per git repository the conversation holds where the agent
 modified files and write_back_mode was enabled on the
 GitRepositoryResource. Omitted for repositories with no changes, local
 folders, or disabled write-back mode.

 Populated during post-run processing. Each entry tracks the
 write-back lifecycle (committed -> pushed -> PR created) and carries
 the PR URL for UI display.

fields.name: SetupProgress
fields.description:
Real-time setup progress reported by the runner during RUN_PENDING.
 Populated progressively as the worker completes setup steps (sandbox init,
 workspace provisioning, skill loading, MCP server connection, etc.).
 Only meaningful while phase == RUN_PENDING. Cleared by the server
 when phase transitions away from PENDING.

fields.name: StreamingUsage
fields.description: Streaming usage summary, updated progressively during the run.

fields.name: FileChangeProgress
fields.description:
Transient, non-authoritative snapshot of the workspace delta accumulating
 during the current turn — the live "N files changed so far" surface, shown
 before any review is possible.

fields.name: FileChanges
fields.description:
The run's file record: the change sets its turns captured, each with the
 files' contents before and after (inline or by storage key), the diff, the
 snapshots they were read from and the consent the turn's commands ran
 under. Empty for a run that changed no file or ran without file review.

 A record only: it carries no status and no decisions. What was decided,
 what is still undecided and what was put back are the session's
 stigmer.file_review.* events.

fields.name: AgentId
fields.description:
ID of the agent this turn ran. Empty when the turn ran the built-in
 assistant, which is not a stored agent.

fields.name: AgentVersionHash
fields.description:
Content hash of the agent version this turn ran (AgentStatus.version_hash
 at create; resolvable through AgentQueryController.getVersion with
 agent_id).

 Empty when agent_id is empty, or when the agent had no recorded version
 at create (an agent last written before agents were versioned, or one
 whose last version failed to archive); such a turn runs the agent as
 it is when the turn starts.

fields.name: LoadedVersions
fields.description:
Every skill and plugin a turn of this run loaded, for the agent and its
 subagents, at the version it loaded. A turn that resumes after a pause
 and loads a newer version adds an entry, so a run that ran two versions
 of one skill lists both. Empty for a run that loaded none, and for runs
 that predate this field.

fields.name: DeclaredPreferences
fields.description:
Standing preferences declared by the organization and the calling user,
 snapshotted into this run at create time.

fields.name: RecalledMemories
fields.description:
The caller's confirmed memories, snapshotted into this run at
 create time: the candidate set the prompt was built from.

fields.name: RunConfig
fields.description:
The settings this turn runs with: spec.run_config (or the saved settings
 of the routine or channel it came through), the defaults of the agent version the
 turn runs, and the lane's operator profile, resolved by RunConfig's rule.

 An empty model_name means no layer named one and the engine chose (the
 native engine's registry default; Cursor's Auto).

fields.name: ApprovalMode
fields.description:
How this turn resolves approval gates: INTERACTIVE or UNATTENDED, never
 UNSPECIFIED.

 A fact of the lane the turn came through, never of the request: a
 routine's turn and the hosted edition's shared-agent guest and channel
 turns are UNATTENDED (nobody is present to approve); every other turn is
 INTERACTIVE.

fields.name: Credentials
fields.description:
Whose logins and secrets this turn uses: decided once when the turn is
 created, and kept when it is recovered.

fields.name: EvalFiles
fields.description: The files an eval case's graders read, as the try's turn left them.

fields.name: StopCause
fields.description:
Why the turn stopped, as one word: budget_reached (the cost cap or the
 tool-call limit), timeout (a stall or the workspace lock), infrastructure
 (the worker shut down or stopped answering), platform_stop, user (a pause
 or a cancel), model_error (the model provider failed the turn), failed
 (any other failure), eval_stopped (an eval case's mock or scaffold
 stopped the try) or review_resolved (a file review was settled). Empty
 while the turn works, and when it ended on its own.

fields.name: MessageFiles
fields.description:
The files this turn's message carried, as content blocks: an image
 block for an image File, a document block for any other, each with a
 file source naming the conversation's own copy. The turn's
 user.message event carries them after its text.

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAudit
statusNestedTypes.description: ApiResourceAudit contains both spec-level and status-level audit details.

fields.name: SpecAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's specification (desired state).

fields.name: StatusAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's status (actual state).

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAuditActor
statusNestedTypes.description:
ApiResourceAuditActor represents the entity that performed an action.

 This is the platform's single actor vocabulary: every "who did this"
 reference (created_by / updated_by, version-history applied_by / pushed_by,
 approval resolved_by_actor) uses this message, so actor rendering is
 uniform across all surfaces.

fields.name: Id
fields.description: Unique identifier of the actor.

fields.name: Avatar
fields.description: URL to the actor's avatar image.

fields.name: DisplayName
fields.description:
Human-readable display name (e.g. "Ada Lovelace"). Empty when unknown;
 renderers fall back to email, then id.

fields.name: Email
fields.description:
Email address of the actor. Empty when unknown or not applicable
 (e.g. machine accounts).

fields.name: MintedBy
fields.description:
The service account whose key minted the user token the actor acted
 through. Empty for every other credential, and on an actor that records
 no act (an account's profile lookup).

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAuditInfo
statusNestedTypes.description: ApiResourceAuditInfo contains detailed audit information.

fields.name: CreatedBy
fields.description: Actor who created this resource.

fields.name: CreatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when the resource was created.

fields.name: UpdatedBy
fields.description: Actor who last updated this resource.

fields.name: UpdatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when the resource was last updated.

fields.name: Event
fields.description: Type of the last event (e.g., "created", "updated").

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceReference
statusNestedTypes.description:
Generic reference to any API resource.
 Used across resources to reference other resources (e.g., Vault, Agent, Skill).
 Canonical written format: "org/slug" (e.g., "acme/web-search", "acme/my-agent").

 A reference has three forms:
 - Written: by name (org and slug), by id, or by both. A write that carries
   both must have them agree, or it is refused naming both. A name is
   resolved to its resource's id when the referring resource is written.
 - Stored: org (the organization's id), kind, id and version. The slug is
   not stored, so a reference keeps pointing at the resource it meant when
   that resource is renamed, and never at a new resource that takes its old
   name after it is deleted.
 - Returned: as stored, with slug filled with the resource's current name.
   A reference whose resource was deleted is returned with an empty slug.

 The kind a reference names is the kind its field declares
 (reference_kind); a reference that carries another kind is refused.

 Every reference in a resource's spec is checked when the resource is
 written: the target must exist, and a target in another organization
 must be one the writing organization's parent shares with its child
 organizations (visibility_child_orgs) to be referenced at all. A blueprint may not be
 more visible than the skills, plugins and agents it references, so
 what a person can run they can also read. A reference that fails the
 check is refused at write, never at run.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization that owns the referenced resource, by slug or id.

 When non-empty: an organization slug (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens,
 starts with a letter, 2-63 characters; e.g. "stigmer", "acme-corp") or an
 organization id (org_<ulid>). The server stores the id, so a stored
 reference keeps pointing at its organization across a rename.

 When empty: the reference is relative — the server resolves it to the parent
 resource's organization at write time. All stored and returned references
 always have org populated (absolute form, the id).

 Use empty org for same-org references (the common case).
 An explicit other org is accepted only when that organization is your
 organization's parent and shares the resource with its children
 (visibility_child_orgs).

fields.name: Kind
fields.description: Kind of the referenced resource (e.g., SKILL, AGENT, PLUGIN).

fields.name: Slug
fields.description:
Resource slug (user-friendly identifier, unique within org).
 Format: lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, must start with a letter
 and end with a letter or digit (e.g., "web-search", "code-reviewer").
 Length: 2-63 characters.

 Written to name the resource; never stored; returned filled with the
 resource's current name, empty when the resource was deleted.

fields.name: Version
fields.description:
The version of a skill, a plugin or a subagent the reference asks for;
 every other kind ignores it.

 Formats:
 - empty or "latest": the latest version;
 - a tag (e.g. "stable", "v1.0"): the version the tag names;
 - a 64-character hash: that exact version, which never changes.

 When it is read: a skill or plugin reference is resolved at the start
 of each turn, so a reference without a hash follows each new push, and
 the run records the version it loaded (RunStatus.loaded_versions). A
 subagent reference is resolved once, when the agent that lists it is
 saved, and the saved reference carries the hash it resolved to.

fields.name: Id
fields.description:
The referenced resource's id: what a stored reference holds. Optional
 on write, where the slug may name the resource instead; an id no
 resource of the kind holds answers as a missing resource. At most 64
 characters.

statusNestedTypes.name: CapturedFileChange
statusNestedTypes.description:
One file's delta within a FileChangeSet.

 Reuses FileContent (inline-or-offload) for before/after and ToolCallOutputRef
 for the offloadable unified diff — no parallel blob types.

fields.name: Id
fields.description:
Stable id of this file change within its set. The id a file-scoped
 stigmer.file_review.decided event names. Never a content hash.

fields.name: PathBefore
fields.description: Path before the change (workspace-root-relative). Empty for ADD.

fields.name: PathAfter
fields.description:
Path after the change (workspace-root-relative). Empty for DELETE; differs
 from path_before for RENAME.

fields.name: Kind
fields.description: The per-file outcome. See FileChangeKind.

fields.name: CaptureClass
fields.description:
How this file was captured (git-tracked vs ignored vs non-git/CAS), which
 governs which substrate holds its before/after bytes. See FileCaptureClass.

fields.name: Before
fields.description: Pre-edit content. Empty for ADD. Large bodies offloaded via FileContent.ref.

fields.name: After
fields.description: Post-edit content. Empty for DELETE. Large bodies offloaded via FileContent.ref.

fields.name: BeforeSha256
fields.description:
SHA-256 of the pre-edit bytes. ENFORCEMENT digest (the reconcile compares
 against the on-disk baseline). Empty for ADD.

fields.name: AfterSha256
fields.description:
SHA-256 of the post-edit bytes. ENFORCEMENT digest (the reconcile applies
 only these exact bytes). Empty for DELETE.

fields.name: UnifiedDiff
fields.description:
Offloadable unified diff for this file. The rendered hunks; large diffs
 spill to the run's storage via the same envelope tool output uses.

fields.name: DiffComplete
fields.description:
False when this file's diff is incomplete (elided, truncated, or not
 capturable). A change set with any diff_complete == false cannot be
 approved as complete — the structural guard against approving an
 unreviewable change.

fields.name: FileDigest
fields.description:
Canonical digest of (path, kind, before, after) for this file. ENFORCEMENT
 only — the per-file analogue of aggregate_digest. Never a correlation key.

fields.name: BlockedReason
fields.description:
The honest cause this file's diff is not fully reviewable, set by the runner
 only when diff_complete == false (otherwise UNSPECIFIED). INFORMATIONAL
 provenance for the review UI — never an enforcement input and never folded
 into file_digest/aggregate_digest. Binary changes are conveyed by
 FileContent.is_binary, not here. See FileReviewBlockReason.

fields.name: LinesAdded
fields.description:
Lines added by this change, computed at capture time by the runner with the
 SAME diff algorithm the SDK renders with, so the list stat and the rendered
 diff can never disagree. INFORMATIONAL display counts only — never an
 enforcement input and never folded into file_digest/aggregate_digest (the
 same contract as blocked_reason). Zero (alongside lines_removed == 0) when
 counting was not possible or meaningful: binary changes, secret-withheld
 entries, oversized sides, and records captured before this field existed.
 Consumers hide the stat in that case rather than showing "+0 -0".

fields.name: LinesRemoved
fields.description: Lines removed by this change. See lines_added for the contract.

statusNestedTypes.name: CasManifestRef
statusNestedTypes.description:
A content-addressed snapshot manifest for paths git cannot capture
 (gitignored or non-git workspaces).

fields.name: ManifestDigest
fields.description: Digest of the manifest listing each captured path and its blob digest.

fields.name: ArtifactUri
fields.description: Storage URI of the stored manifest.

statusNestedTypes.name: ContentBlock
statusNestedTypes.description:
ContentBlock is one block of an event's content: text, an image, a
 document, or a redacted block.

 The fields are those of Claude Managed Agents' content blocks; type names
 the block and only that block's fields are set.

fields.name: Type
fields.description: The block's kind: text, image, document or redacted.

fields.name: Text
fields.description: The text of a text block.

fields.name: Source
fields.description: Where an image or document block's bytes come from.

fields.name: Context
fields.description: Context about a document block, for the model.

fields.name: Title
fields.description: A document block's title.

statusNestedTypes.name: ContentSource
statusNestedTypes.description:
ContentSource says where an image or document block's bytes come from:
 inline base64 data, inline plain text, a URL, or an uploaded file.

fields.name: Type
fields.description: The source's kind: base64, text, url or file.

fields.name: Data
fields.description: The inline data of a base64 or text source.

fields.name: MediaType
fields.description: The media type of inline data, for example image/png or text/plain.

fields.name: Url
fields.description: The address of a url source.

fields.name: FileId
fields.description: The uploaded file of a file source.

statusNestedTypes.name: DeclaredPreferences
statusNestedTypes.description:
DeclaredPreferences carries the standing preference texts injected into
 this run's prompt, one field per declaring scope.

fields.name: OrgContext
fields.description: The organization's standing context, verbatim.

fields.name: UserContext
fields.description: The calling user's standing context, verbatim.

statusNestedTypes.name: EvalFile
statusNestedTypes.description: EvalFile is one file's content after the turn.

fields.name: Path
fields.description: The path as the case's graders name it.

fields.name: Text
fields.description: The file's text.

fields.name: Binary
fields.description: The file is not text.

fields.name: Absent
fields.description: Nothing is at the path.

fields.name: Unreadable
fields.description:
The file could not be read, and why (too large, not a regular file,
 outside the workspace).

statusNestedTypes.name: EvalFiles
statusNestedTypes.description:
EvalFiles is the content, after an eval try's turn, of each
 file its case's graders read (EvalCaseContext.read_files).

fields.name: Files
fields.description: Each file, once, in the order read_files names them.

statusNestedTypes.name: FileChangeProgress
statusNestedTypes.description:
A transient, non-authoritative snapshot of the workspace delta accumulating
 during the CURRENT turn — the live "N files changed so far" surface.

fields.name: ChangeSetId
fields.description:
Id of the change set this progress previews ("${executionId}:${turnSeq}"),
 before it is captured. A stale prior-turn snapshot is cleared once the next
 turn pins a new baseline.

fields.name: FilesChanged
fields.description:
Total number of files changed so far this turn. The honest total: it may
 exceed entries.length when the entry list is capped for a very large turn.

fields.name: LinesAdded
fields.description:
Total lines added / removed across all changed files this turn. Zero when
 uncountable (binary / secret-withheld). INFORMATIONAL display only — never an
 enforcement input (progress has no digests).

fields.name: Entries
fields.description:
The per-file entries (slim: no bodies, no digests, no diffs). May be a capped
 prefix of the full change list; files_changed carries the true total.

fields.name: CapturedAt
fields.description: When this snapshot was taken (RFC3339). Presentation-only; never a digest input.

statusNestedTypes.name: FileChangeProgressEntry
statusNestedTypes.description: One file within a FileChangeProgress snapshot — a slim, non-authoritative row.

fields.name: PathBefore
fields.description: Path before the change (workspace-root-relative). Empty for ADD.

fields.name: PathAfter
fields.description: Path after the change (workspace-root-relative). Empty for DELETE.

fields.name: Kind
fields.description: The per-file outcome. See FileChangeKind.

fields.name: LinesAdded
fields.description:
Lines added by this change. Zero (alongside lines_removed == 0) when counting
 was not possible or meaningful (binary / secret) — consumers hide the stat
 rather than show "+0 -0" (the same contract as CapturedFileChange.lines_added).

fields.name: LinesRemoved
fields.description: Lines removed by this change. See lines_added for the contract.

statusNestedTypes.name: FileChangeSet
statusNestedTypes.description:
The set of file deltas produced by one agent turn, reviewed and reconciled
 as a unit.

 A record of what the turn changed: the files' contents before and after,
 the snapshots they were read from and the consent the turn's commands ran
 under. It carries no state and no decisions; the session's
 stigmer.file_review.* events say what was kept, what was undone and what is
 still open.

fields.name: Id
fields.description:
Stable id of this change set, unique per turn. The id the session's
 stigmer.file_review.* events name. Never a content hash.

fields.name: TurnId
fields.description: Id of the turn that produced this change set.

fields.name: HarnessId
fields.description:
Harness that produced the edits: "cursor" | "deep-agent". Carried for audit
 and so the reconcile adapter knows which harness lifecycle authored the set.

fields.name: BaselineSnapshot
fields.description:
Workspace state captured at turn start — the "before" the authoritative
 diff is computed against.

fields.name: CandidateSnapshot
fields.description:
Workspace state captured at the turn boundary — the "after". The authoritative
 diff is diff(baseline_snapshot, candidate_snapshot); no streamed args, no
 pre-execution proposal is ever authoritative.

fields.name: Changes
fields.description: The per-file deltas in this change set (the rendered review surface).

fields.name: AggregateDigest
fields.description:
Canonical digest over the ordered change manifest. ENFORCEMENT only: lets
 the reconcile refuse to apply a manifest that differs from what was
 reviewed. Never a correlation key.

fields.name: DiffCompleteness
fields.description:
Whether the rendered diff is complete enough to approve safely, a rollup
 over the per-file changes. COMPLETE is approvable as-is; BINARY_SUMMARY_ONLY
 (binary is the set's only blocker) is keepable in one shot via an
 acknowledged CHANGE_SET approve; PARTIAL_BLOCKED must be resolved per file.
 An honest UI/audit signal — the backend gate re-derives keep-all from the
 per-file changes, never trusting this value. See DiffCompleteness.

fields.name: CommandProvenance
fields.description:
The consent the turn's commands ran under, when every change in the set
 came from a command a person had allowed. Absent otherwise.

statusNestedTypes.name: FileContent
statusNestedTypes.description:
One side (before or after) of a file's content.

 Small bodies are carried inline; large bodies are offloaded to the run's
 storage and referenced via the existing tool-output offload envelope. Exactly
 one of inline or ref is set; when offloaded, the head preview lives in
 ref.truncated_preview and the full size in ref.size_bytes.

fields.name: Inline
fields.description: Full UTF-8 content, inline. Set only when under the inline cap.

fields.name: Ref
fields.description:
Offload pointer for large content; reuses the tool-output offload
 envelope (storage_key, size_bytes, content_hash, truncated_preview).

fields.name: IsBinary
fields.description:
True when this side is binary; clients skip text diffing and render
 "binary file changed" instead.

statusNestedTypes.name: GitTreeRef
statusNestedTypes.description: A git no-commit tree snapshot (write-tree + a stigmer-namespaced ref).

fields.name: TreeOid
fields.description: The tree object id produced by git write-tree.

fields.name: Ref
fields.description:
The ref the snapshot is pinned under, e.g.
 "refs/stigmer/{run}/{baseline|candidate|approved}". Keeps the
 snapshot reachable (un-GC'd) without a commit on any user branch.

statusNestedTypes.name: LoadedVersions
statusNestedTypes.description:
LoadedVersions lists what a run loaded besides its agent: one list per
 kind, each entry a reference to the exact version that ran.

fields.name: Skills
fields.description:
Skills, each at its version hash (SkillStatus.version_hash). The version
 is empty only for a skill whose last version failed to archive, which
 loads as it is.

fields.name: Plugins
fields.description:
Plugins, each at its archive's digest (PluginStatus.digest). A plugin's
 own skills, servers and hooks are named by its digest.

statusNestedTypes.name: RecalledMemories
statusNestedTypes.description:
RecalledMemories is the server-composed snapshot of the caller's
 confirmed memories for one run — the candidate set for prompt
 injection.

fields.name: Enabled
fields.description: Whether memory is enabled for this run's caller.

fields.name: Facts
fields.description:
The confirmed facts — every confirmed memory of the caller in this
 organization, the candidate set for prompt injection.

statusNestedTypes.name: RecalledMemoryFact
statusNestedTypes.description:
RecalledMemoryFact is one confirmed memory as injected into an
 run.

fields.name: MemoryId
fields.description: ID of the memory record this fact came from.

fields.name: Content
fields.description: The remembered fact, verbatim as stored at snapshot time.

statusNestedTypes.name: RunConfig
statusNestedTypes.description:
RunConfig is the settings message for every run: a model, a speed tier,
 thinking, and run bounds.

 The same message is a message's request (RunSpec.run_config),
 the saved settings of a routine (its invocation) or a channel,
 an agent author's defaults (AgentSpec.run_config,
 versioned with the agent), and the settings a turn ran with
 (RunStatus.run_config). Zero or empty means "not set at this
 layer".

 The server resolves a turn's settings once, at create, from three layers,
 most specific first: the message (or the routine or channel it came
 through), the
 agent's defaults, and the lane's operator profile.

 - Choices. model_name comes from the first layer that names one. When no
   layer names one, the model is left to the engine (the native engine's
   registry default; Cursor's Auto). service_tier and thinking_mode each
   come from the first layer, at or above the model's layer, that sets
   them: a less specific layer's tier or thinking was chosen for another
   model, so it never lands on this one. Without a model, tier and thinking
   come only from the message.
 - Bounds. max_cost_usd, max_tool_rounds and max_tool_result_chars each take
   the smallest positive value any layer sets. An operator profile is a
   ceiling the message, the routine or channel, and the agent can lower
   but never raise.
 - The agent's choices apply only on the engine its defaults name
   (AgentSpec.harness). On a conversation running the other engine the
   agent layer gives its bounds alone.

 Saved settings are self-contained: a routine, channel or agent that sets
 service_tier FAST or thinking_mode ENABLED names the model it is for. Only a
 message may set them alone, to adjust the model it is given.

fields.name: ModelName
fields.description: The model each run uses. Example: "claude-sonnet-4-6".

fields.name: MaxCostUsd
fields.description:
Maximum estimated cost in USD per run.

 When the run's estimated spend reaches this limit, the run stops with a
 "send another message to continue" prompt and ends TERMINATED; the work
 done so far is kept. The limit is checked each time the engine reports
 its spend, so a run can end somewhat above it. The native harness
 reports after every model call, counts a subagent's spend toward the
 limit, and advises the agent to wrap up at about 80% of the budget; the
 Cursor harness gives no warning.

 0 = not set at this layer. The budget is per message: a follow-up
 message, or a run resuming after an approval, starts a fresh count; a
 run continuing after a restart, a lost runner or a stall keeps its
 count. The
 spend is the runner's estimate, reported on
 RunStatus.streaming_usage.estimated_cost_usd, not the billed
 amount.

fields.name: MaxToolRounds
fields.description:
Maximum model-to-tools reasoning cycles per message.

 A round is one model response that proposes one or more tool calls,
 followed by their execution; parallel tool calls in one response are one
 round. When the limit is reached the run stops with a "send another
 message to continue" prompt, and the work done so far is kept. The agent
 is advised to wrap up at about 80% of the budget.

 0 = not set at this layer; with no layer setting it the agent runs until
 the task completes or loop detection stops a repetitive pattern. When
 set, the valid range is 10–1000; values outside it are clamped to the
 nearest bound. The budget is per message: a follow-up message, or a run
 resuming after an approval, starts a fresh count. Subagent rounds are
 not counted, and the Cursor harness does not enforce this field.

fields.name: ServiceTier
fields.description:
Service tier for each run's model calls: standard (the default) or fast, where fast bills at the model's fast-tier rates and requires a model that offers one.

 UNSPECIFIED is not set at this layer; with no layer setting it the run
 uses STANDARD, never the provider account default. FAST is valid only
 for a model whose registry entry declares a fast pricing variant on the
 engine that runs it; validated fail-closed on the resolved settings at
 create.

fields.name: ThinkingMode
fields.description:
Thinking mode for each run's model calls: disabled (the default) or
 enabled, where enabled selects the model's extended-reasoning variant
 (billed at base per-token rates — reasoning tokens bill as output).

 UNSPECIFIED is not set at this layer; with no layer setting it the run
 uses DISABLED, never the provider account default. ENABLED is valid only
 for a model whose registry entry declares the thinking capability on the
 engine that runs it; validated fail-closed on the resolved settings at
 create. Combines freely with service_tier.

fields.name: MaxToolResultChars
fields.description:
Maximum number of characters for a single tool result before truncation.
 A longer result reaches the agent as its start and its end, with a line
 between them saying how much was left out. The whole result is kept for
 the session, outside the workspace, and the line says where, so the
 agent reads the rest back instead of running the tool again; a tool that
 pages itself (reading a file, searching, listing, fetching a page) keeps
 no copy, and the line says how to narrow the call instead.

 0 = not set at this layer; with no layer setting it the platform default
 applies (30,000 chars, about 7,500 tokens). Applies to every tool result,
 a subagent's included; the Cursor harness does not read this field.

statusNestedTypes.name: RunCredentials
statusNestedTypes.description: RunCredentials records whose logins and secrets a turn uses.

fields.name: Person
fields.description:
The person whose turn this is, by identity account id. Absent for a
 turn no person sent: a routine's, a channel's (a chat-link guest's
 included), an app user's or a machine account's, which use only the
 vaults their session and their routine, channel or embedding settings
 name.

fields.name: Sources
fields.description:
Where each value the turn uses lives: one entry per key and declarer,
 naming a vault and an entry, never a value. A runner fetches the
 values from these vaults when the turn's work starts
 (VaultValueController.fetchValues). An optional key nothing holds has
 no entry.

statusNestedTypes.name: RunValueDeclarer
statusNestedTypes.description: RunValueDeclarer names who declared a value a turn uses.

fields.name: Kind
fields.description: Agent, tool, plugin or repository.

fields.name: Name
RepositoryUrl
fields.description: The repository's URL; empty for an agent, a tool or a plugin.

fields.name: PluginId
fields.description:
The plugin that declared it: a plugin's tool's plugin, or the plugin
 whose hooks read it; empty for everything else.

fields.name: Server
fields.description:
The tool's server name in its plugin or its agent; empty for everything
 else.

fields.name: PluginDigest
fields.description:
The archive of the tool's plugin this run planned (the plugin's
 digest); empty for everything else. The values fetch reads the server
 at that version, so a run of a pinned version keeps its tools when the
 plugin is pushed again.

fields.name: AgentId
fields.description: The agent whose own server the tool is; empty for everything else.

fields.name: AgentVersion
fields.description:
The version of that agent this run planned (its version hash); empty
 for everything else. The values fetch reads the server at that version,
 so a run of a pinned version keeps the address it planned when the
 agent is edited.

statusNestedTypes.name: RunValueSource
statusNestedTypes.description: RunValueSource says where one value a turn uses lives. It names no value.

fields.name: Key
fields.description: The environment variable.

fields.name: Declarer
fields.description: Who declared it.

fields.name: Origin
fields.description: Where it lives.

fields.name: VaultId
fields.description:
The vault holding it; empty for a repository's own token and a
 declaration's default.

fields.name: Entry
fields.description:
The entry: a secret's name, a login's address, or the repository
 entry's name for its own token; empty for a declaration's default.

fields.name: Login
fields.description:
Whether the entry is a login (a connection at an address) rather than a
 secret by name. A sign-in among them is renewed when it is fetched, as
 the vault records it then.

fields.name: PlainValue
fields.description:
A declaration's own plain default, the one value a manifest holds: it
 is a fixed setting of the agent or tool, never a secret.

statusNestedTypes.name: SetupProgress
statusNestedTypes.description: Setup progress reported during the RUN_PENDING phase.

fields.name: CurrentPhase
fields.description:
Human-readable label for the current setup phase.
 Examples: "Initializing sandbox…", "Setting up workspace…", "Loading skills…"
 Empty when setup phase reporting has not started or is complete.

statusNestedTypes.name: SnapshotRef
statusNestedTypes.description:
An immutable pointer to a captured workspace state.

 One of git / cas is set per kind; HYBRID carries both (git-tracked files via
 the tree ref, ignored/non-git files via the CAS manifest). Snapshots are
 captured by the runner and are idempotent under Temporal retries.

fields.name: Kind
fields.description: Which substrate holds this snapshot. See SnapshotKind.

fields.name: Git
fields.description: Git no-commit tree reference; set when kind is GIT_TREE_REF or HYBRID.

fields.name: Cas
fields.description:
Content-addressed manifest reference for ignored/non-git paths; set when
 kind is CAS_MANIFEST or HYBRID.

statusNestedTypes.name: StreamingUsageSummary
statusNestedTypes.description:
Accumulated token usage from execution worker turn-ended events.
 Carried on RunStatus.streaming_usage for real-time streaming UX.

fields.name: InputTokens
fields.description: Accumulated input tokens across all turns.

fields.name: OutputTokens
fields.description: Accumulated output tokens across all turns.

fields.name: CacheReadTokens
fields.description: Accumulated cache-read tokens across all turns.

fields.name: CacheWriteTokens
fields.description: Accumulated cache-write tokens across all turns.

fields.name: TotalTokens
fields.description:
Total tokens across all turns: input_tokens + output_tokens. The Cursor
 SDK reports input_tokens cache-inclusive (cache_read/cache_write are
 subsets of it), so the cache buckets are NOT added again here.

fields.name: TurnCount
fields.description: Number of completed turns observed.

fields.name: EstimatedCostUsd
fields.description:
Estimated cost in USD computed from the runner-side rate card (the
 providers' list prices): the working number of the run's cost cap
 (RunConfig.max_cost_usd). No usage report reads it.

fields.name: Model
fields.description: Model identifier the runner requested for this run's turns.

fields.name: ObservedAt
fields.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last turn-ended event observed.

fields.name: RequestedServiceTier
fields.description:
Service tier the runner requested for this run's model calls.

 Always explicit once the runner has translated the turn's settings
 (STANDARD when RunStatus.run_config.service_tier was unset) — the audit
 record that the account default was never left in control.

fields.name: RequestedModelParams
fields.description:
JSON-encoded provider variant parameters the runner sent with the model
 selection (Cursor ModelSelection.params, e.g.
 [{"id":"fast","value":"false"}]). Empty when the harness sent none.

fields.name: RequestedThinkingMode
fields.description:
Thinking mode the runner requested for this run's model calls.

 Always explicit once the runner has translated the turn's settings
 (DISABLED when RunStatus.run_config.thinking_mode was unset) — the audit
 record that the account default was never left in control
 (stigmer/stigmer#772; several catalog defaults are thinking=true).

statusNestedTypes.name: ToolCallOutputRef
statusNestedTypes.description:
ToolCallOutputRef points to content the runner offloaded to the run's
 storage: a tool call's full output, or one side of a captured file change
 too large to keep inline.

 This is deliberately not a File (what an agent saves for the person to
 download): an output ref is internal spillover of a tool's result, not a
 deliverable. The bytes live in the server's file storage (R2 in the cloud,
 a local disk otherwise); only this reference is persisted in the run status.

fields.name: StorageKey
fields.description:
Storage location of the full output bytes.
 Format: "artifacts/{run_id}/toolcalls/{tool_call_id}.{ext}"

 Clients resolve the bytes/URL on demand from this stable key (via
 getArtifactContent or getArtifactDownloadUrl) — there is deliberately no
 persisted URL, since a pre-signed URL would expire while the reference does
 not.

fields.name: SizeBytes
fields.description: Size in bytes of the full (original, pre-truncation) output.

fields.name: ContentHash
fields.description:
SHA-256 hex digest of the full output bytes. Lets the runner dedupe
 uploads (skip re-uploading identical content across repeated persists) and
 lets clients invalidate caches when content changes under a stable key.

fields.name: MimeType
fields.description:
MIME type of the offloaded content.
 Examples: "image/png", "text/plain", "application/json".

fields.name: IsImage
fields.description:
True when the offloaded content is an image the UI should render inline
 (e.g. a screenshot from a computer-use MCP server).

fields.name: TruncatedPreview
fields.description:
Short head of the original text content, kept inline for an at-a-glance
 preview without fetching the full output. Empty for image content.

statusNestedTypes.name: TurnCommandProvenance
statusNestedTypes.description:
The runner's turn facts backing the approved-command auto-keep policy:
 its assertion that EVERY mutation in the candidate was produced by
 executed shell commands the human had already authorized, with the consent
 evidence the backend can verify.

fields.name: ConsentToolCallIds
fields.description:
Ids of the tool calls whose answers in the session's log authorize this
 turn's executed commands: the call a person allowed, or the call whose
 grant for its class covered the command. Exact-id lookup — never a content
 or fuzzy match. Empty only when authorized_by_auto_approve_all carries the
 consent instead.

fields.name: AuthorizedByAutoApproveAll
fields.description:
True when the commands ran ungated under the pre-armed
 spec.auto_approve_all global bypass (there is no per-command consent row to
 cite). The backend verifies this against the spec field it owns.

statusNestedTypes.name: WorkspaceWriteBack
statusNestedTypes.description:
WorkspaceWriteBack captures the outcome of the platform-owned git
 write-back workflow for a single repository resource.

 One entry is created per git repository that had uncommitted changes
 when the run reached a terminal phase. Not populated for local folders or
 repositories with no detected changes.

 The write-back progresses through phases: committed -> pushed ->
 pr_created. If any step fails, the phase is set to FAILED with the
 error message, and processing continues to the next repository.
 One failed write-back does not block others.

fields.name: WorkspaceEntryName
fields.description:
Name of the repository resource this write-back corresponds to.
 Links to SessionSpec.resources[].name.
 Example: "my-app", "frontend"

fields.name: BranchName
fields.description:
Branch created for the agent's changes.
 Format: "stigmer/{short_run_id}"
 Example: "stigmer/a1b2c3d4"

fields.name: BaseBranch
fields.description:
Base branch the PR targets (the branch that was originally cloned).
 Example: "main", "develop"

fields.name: CommitSha
fields.description:
Full commit SHA of the agent's changes on the branch.
 Example: "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924"

fields.name: PullRequestUrl
fields.description:
GitHub pull request URL.
 Empty when write-back mode is not PR-based or PR creation failed.
 Example: "https://github.com/acme/my-app/pull/42"

fields.name: PullRequestNumber
fields.description:
GitHub pull request number.
 0 when no PR was created.

fields.name: DiffSummary
fields.description:
Human-readable summary of changes from `git diff --stat`.
 Example: "3 files changed, 42 insertions(+), 7 deletions(-)"

fields.name: Phase
fields.description: Current phase of the write-back workflow.

fields.name: Error
fields.description:
Error message if the write-back failed at any step.
 Empty on success.
